question: The sea is of vital importance for the EU. According to the ΟECD1, its political and economic importance is increasing rapidly because it impacts the food chain, transport networks, renewable energy sources and tourism. At the same time, it has a strong geopolitical dimension, because within the maritime zones of the 27 Member States the EU is increasing its regional strength.

The conditions for exercising rights at sea have been codified by the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). The Commission has already developed the European MSP Platform for maritime spatial planning2, based on the Seville Map3.

However, in the fluid geopolitical environment of the Eastern Mediterranean, European rights, which are identical to those of the Member States, are being called into question or threatened by revisionist powers such as Türkiye4.

Since the developments in Syria, with the pending talks on the declaration of a Türkiye-Syria EEZ (modelled on the illegal and abusive agreement between Türkiye and Libya)5, pose a serious risk of loss of geopolitical and economic power on the part of the EU: 1.

Does the Commission intend to develop a unified strategy for maritime planning and maritime zones, in terms of both coordination and sanctions against third countries, given the challenges and threats against Member States such as Greece and Cyprus?
Does it intend to go ahead with the adoption of a ‘European EEZ’, on the basis of the Seville Map, protecting the vital maritime rights of the EU and its Member States?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (28.2.2025) 1. The Maritime Spatial Planning (MSP) Directive (2014/89/EU)1 requires coastal Member States to adopt their maritime spatial plans by 31 March 2021. The Commission is committed to fostering enhanced coordination among Member States to ensure the sustainable management of maritime areas.

This includes working towards coherent MSP across the EU, as required by the Directive. Article 52 of the Treaty on European Union (TEU) and 355 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) define the territorial scope of the EU Treaties by reference to the territories of Member States.

In accordance with the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), it is for each coastal State to establish and delimitate its maritime zones (including with other States in case of adjacent waters). The EU has no competence regarding the establishment/proclamation and delimitation of maritime zones. 2.

The Seville Charter is a regional map created by an external party, which holds no legal significance. The adoption of a ‘European Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ)’ by the EU is neither planned nor possible.

While the delimitation of the EEZ is a matter falling under the competence of the Member States, in case of unilateral actions or provocations in breach of international law by a third country or countries, the EU will use all the instruments and the options at its disposal, including in accordance with Article 29 TEU and Article 215 TFEU, in order to defend its interests and those of the Member States2.
